Playbook.name: FortiGate — Internal Host Communicating with a High-Risk/Sanctioned Country - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An internal host made an ACCEPTED connection to a high-risk/sanctioned country (Iran, Russia, etc.) - first-seen for this (host,country) via new_terms. Triage question: is this unexpected communication with a sanctioned destination (C2/exfil or compliance breach), or legitimate business traffic?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: For a bank, connections to sanctioned countries carry both security (C2/exfil) and regulatory/compliance risk.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate perimeter and internal firewalls (HQ + DR)
Internal server and user segments behind the FortiGate

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate logs shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-fortinet_fortigate.* (verified live).

Fields: fortinet.firewall.subtype (ips/dns/...), fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.severity, fortinet.firewall.attack, fortinet.firewall.srccountry/dstcountry ('Reserved' = RFC1918 internal), fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, dns.question.name, source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port.

Signal.Name: High-risk country comms
Signal.Details: internal source, action accept, dstcountry in the high-risk set; first-seen (host,country).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Business may have legitimate ties (correspondent banking, remittance) to some listed countries; unexpected host-to-sanctioned-country traffic, especially from a workstation/server with no such role, is the concern.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the sanctioned-country communication is expected business traffic or unexpected C2/exfil/compliance-relevant activity.

Step.name: Connection detail - destination, ports, volume
Step.Purpose: See what the host connected to, on which ports, and how much data-shaped the traffic is.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND fortinet.firewall.action == "accept" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), dsts = VALUES(destination.ip), dports = VALUES(destination.port), dcountries = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry) BY fortinet.firewall.dstcountry | SORT conns DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: Web ports (443) to a CDN edge in a listed country may be benign; non-standard ports, large sustained transfers, or direct-IP connections to sanctioned countries are concerning.

Step.name: What is this host and does it have a business reason
Step.Purpose: A SWIFT/correspondent-banking server may legitimately talk internationally; a user workstation should not reach sanctioned countries.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.traffic-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS total = COUNT(*), countries = COUNT_DISTINCT(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry), country_list = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.dstcountry) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A host talking to many countries may be a proxy/gateway; a workstation reaching only the one sanctioned country is more suspicious. Correlate the IP with its role/segment.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows sustained/large or non-web connections to the sanctioned country from a host with no business role for it.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unexpected Sanctioned-Country Comms - escalate to IR + compliance)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the traffic is web (443) to a CDN edge that merely geolocates to a listed country, from a normal browsing host.
INV-02 shows the host is a documented international-banking gateway with a business reason.
Unexpected comms but business justification cannot be confirmed.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FGHR-CONN, INV-02-FGHR-HOST to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Geo/CDN artifact or legitimate business communication.

Indicators.Item: Web traffic to a CDN edge that geolocates to a listed country.
Host is a documented international gateway.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the destination is a benign CDN/business partner.
Document; add (host,country) to the learned baseline; close.

TruePositive.Definition: C2/exfiltration or unauthorised communication with a sanctioned destination.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; capture the connection detail; open IR.
Notify compliance/AML (sanctions relevance); block the destination.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured proxy/route sending traffic through a listed country unintentionally.

Indicators.Item: A routing/proxy misconfig geolocating traffic to a listed country.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Assess the destination and host role.
If unexpected: isolate the host and notify IR + compliance.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Scope the communication; check for exfil; eradicate if C2.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce geo-blocking for sanctioned countries except approved business flows; monitor exceptions.

QualityChecks.Check: new_terms keys on (host, dstcountry) - legitimate business pairs fire once then learn. 'Reserved' src = internal.
Compliance/AML has a parallel interest - route confirmed sanctioned comms to them.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Geo/CDN artifact or business flow confirmed; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host isolated; no exfil/C2; compliance notified; destination blocked.
